definition: Relinquish means to give up or let go of a possession, position, right, or control — often formally, and often reluctantly.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word relinquish. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know relinquish should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After her third ankle injury, Marisol agreed to relinquish the team captaincy so a healthier teammate could lead the squad.
Yield is milder than relinquish: a driver who yields at an intersection gives way for a moment and then moves on.
Forfeit is stronger than relinquish: a team that forfeits a match loses it outright as a penalty, with no say in the matter.

Surrender means to give something up under pressure — an opponent or circumstance has forced the choice, as when an army surrenders a city. Relinquish is quieter: you let go of a post, right, or grip, often reluctantly but not necessarily defeated. A cornered army surrenders; a retiring chair relinquishes the gavel.

Cede means to formally yield something to another party, especially territory or power, usually by treaty or agreement — an empire cedes islands. Relinquish needs no recipient and no negotiation: you can relinquish a claim, a license, or your grip on a rope with nobody taking it over.

Waive means to voluntarily decline to enforce a right, fee, or requirement — a bank waives a fee. What is waived is set aside before it is ever used. Relinquish means letting go of something already in your hands: control, a seat, a grip. You waive a claim before exercising it; you relinquish what you hold.

Alvarez finally agreed to relinquish his driver's license after his doctor explained how much his eyesight had declined.
Alvarez gives up a privilege he has held for decades, formally and reluctantly — exactly the kind of letting-go that relinquish describes.
Relinquish is about letting go of something you actually hold — control, a claim, a seat, even a physical grip ("he relinquished his hold on the rope").
It often suggests reluctance or formality.
Its unit-mate renunciation is a more deliberate, often public rejection of a belief or claim: you relinquish the wheel, but you announce a renunciation of a throne.

For forty-one years, Edna Marsh climbed the eighty-nine steps of the Point Alder light, and for forty-one years she refused every suggestion that she stop.
When the coast guard automated the lamp, it did not force her out; her contract let her stay on as caretaker for life.
Instead, at a small ceremony last June, she chose to relinquish the keeper's post herself, setting the brass key on the logbook she had kept since 1984.
"Nobody took this from me," she told the crowd.
"I am setting it down while my hands are still steady." The post will remain vacant; the town plans no replacement, and the key now rests in the harbor museum beside her final log entry.
